name: Kharam Naga
catalog_citation: Singh, Khaidem Dutta. 2014. A Descriptive Study of Kharam: An Endangered Language of Northeastern India. PhD thesis, Department of Linguistics, Assam University, Silchar (guide: Kh. Dhiren Singha). 243 pp. Shodhganga, hdl:10603/84205 (chapters as separate bitstreams).
catalog_locator: Singh 2014, Ch. III 'Phonology', sec. 3.1 'Phonemic Inventory', p. 12 and sec. 3.2 'Tones', p. 14; restated verbatim in the Abstract and in Ch. VI 'Conclusion' item (v), p. 150.
catalog_quote: [p. 12, sec. 3.1 Phonemic Inventory] There are twenty six (26) phonemes in Kharam. Out of which, twenty four (24) phonemes are segmental and two (2) are supra-segmental. ... (B) Supra-segmental phonemes Tones (2) a. High tone b. Low tone [p. 14, sec. 3.2 Tones] Like the majority of Sino-Tibetan languages, Kharam is a tonal language in which a change in the pitch of the syllable corresponds to a change in its meaning. Kharam has two contrastive lexical tones: high and low. However the analysis of tones is not extensive in this present study and the further research is required to draw the exhaustive tonal structure of the language. ... /pá/ ‘father’ /pà/ ‘mushroom’ /tú/ ‘who’ /tù/ ‘feed’
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress
sweep_summary: Kharam Naga (khar1288) is not in the catalog. The single title-keyword hit in the list of works with stress in the title (Christou & Baltazani 2010, stressed vowels in the Greek dialect of Kato Pedina) is a Glottolog computational mis-assignment ('kato and the'), concerns Modern Greek, and is irrelevant; not downloaded. The only first-hand description of Kharam, Singh 2014 (Assam University PhD, held by the project from the earlier reading at, treats the language as tonal (two lexical tones, high/low, ch. III p. 12-14) and contains no statement on word stress or accent (zero hits for stress/accent across all chapters). Haokip 2011 (LTBA) has no phonology for Kharam. sources.locator: ch. III Phonology, sec. 3.1 p. 12 and sec. 3.2 'Tones' p. 14
sources.note: The only phonological description of Kharam. Ch. III sec. 3.1 (p. 12) lists two suprasegmental phonemes, both tones; sec. 3.2 (p. 14) describes two contrastive lexical tones (high/low) with minimal pairs pa 'father'/'mushroom', tu 'who'/'feed'. A a full-text search for stress/accent every chapter text for 'stress' and 'accent' returns zero hits; the thesis makes no statement about word-stress placement. Silent on stress; describes the language as tonal.

sources.note: Ethnologue reports high mutual intelligibility between Kharam and Purum (puru1266); a Purum sketch with a suprasegmental section would be the nearest proxy, but it is a different glottocode and cannot stand in for khar1288 in the catalog.

sources.note: Kharam is not among the 117 SPPEL languages (related Purum, Koireng, Chothe, Tarao, Aimol, Moyon, Lamgang are); no Kharam sketch exists there.
